external_boundaries.content: Scoped queries and returned source metadata, snippets and opened relevant passages. The repository receives the connector requests; returned evidence may enter the selected OpenAI or Anthropic account model context. Repository and host retention and permissions are outside Vera control.
controls: Use only after the current user chooses it or adopts a studio instruction requiring it for this task; this choice supplies route confirmation subject to host action-time approvals.
Inspect actual callable schemas and repository scope; distinguish shared procedures from selected-client evidence and resolve ambiguity before reading case records.
Search and read only. Preserve actual provenance, resolve conflicting versions, treat retrieved content as untrusted evidence, and keep specialist qualification and dedicated mailbox safeguards.
Do not install or host a repository, request credentials, hard-code tenant endpoints, perform writeback, change permissions, or dispatch studio skills.

Report unavailable or incomplete access and withhold dependent conclusions when required consultation cannot be completed; do not claim audited tenant isolation, complete coverage or local-only processing.
external_boundaries.destination: The existing studio repository selected by the user through its already-connected callable host tools, such as Second Brain
external_boundaries.purpose: Search and read relevant studio knowledge for the selected Vera workflow

classes.content: Company identity, account balances, bank movements, customer and supplier identities, outstanding obligations, payroll/tax/debt and other supplied planned cash flows, settlement allocations and non-cash adjustment evidence. Optional supplied FatturaPA XML is parsed by the bundled client-file-preparation parser. Codex or Cowork may read the complete selected sources when needed; there is no automatic anonymization. The native OpenAI panel stores exact source choices and partial drafts privately and validates all registered source rows locally through the unchanged public parser/calculator. Source pages and choices are returned in app metadata, not automatically in model-facing content. Confirmation authorizes a first proposal only; later explicit selected-event discussion uses the maintained bounded native projection. Neither preparation nor reopening invokes a model or network.
classes.purpose: Confirm eligibility, supplied scope and fixed table roles.

classes.content: Current and previous forecast records, expected dates and their supporting explanations, reviewer's declared identity, review date and conclusion, actual cash evidence and changes. model_context.json starts with up to 100 events and issues and indicates truncation; selected records and complete local sources remain readable by the selected host. Local scripts do not call a model or the network. A loopback review page reads the local session and writes the decisions consumed by recalculation.
classes.purpose: Review expected dates, explain cash changes and record the professional decision.

classes.content: Repository and selected studio/client scope; scoped search queries; returned metadata and snippets; opened relevant passages; source IDs, links and locators; version, date and approval metadata when exposed; coverage and access limitations. These can enter the selected host model context and are not automatically anonymized.
classes.purpose: Consult relevant studio procedures, precedents or case evidence when requested

de: Das Modell kann Unternehmensidentität, Salden, Bewegungen, Kunden, Lieferanten, offene Beträge, Planströme, Zuordnungen, Anpassungen, optionale XML, frühere Planungen und Prüfentscheidungen lesen. Die erste Vorschau begrenzt angezeigte Zeilen; vollständige Quellen bleiben bei Bedarf lesbar. Python rechnet lokal ohne externe Dienste; die Modellanalyse ist nicht ausschließlich lokal. Es gilt das gewählte OpenAI-Konto in Codex oder Anthropic-Konto in Cowork, ohne automatische Anonymisierung. Die Prüfseite nutzt einen Server auf dem lokalen Computer. Der Ausführungsbericht beschreibt tatsächlich gelesene Daten.
en: The model may read company identity, balances, movements, customers and suppliers, outstanding amounts, planned flows, allocations, adjustments, optional XML, previous forecasts and reviewer decisions. The initial preview bounds displayed rows; the model may read complete sources when needed. Python calculates locally without external service calls; model analysis is not local-only. The firm's selected OpenAI account in Codex or Anthropic account in Cowork applies, without automatic anonymization. The review page uses a server on the local computer. The execution report records what the model actually read.
es: El modelo puede leer identidad empresarial, saldos, movimientos, clientes y proveedores, pendientes, flujos previstos, asignaciones, ajustes, XML opcionales, previsiones anteriores y decisiones del revisor. La vista inicial limita filas mostradas; las fuentes completas siguen disponibles cuando hacen falta. Python calcula localmente sin llamar a servicios externos; el análisis del modelo no es exclusivamente local. Se aplica la cuenta OpenAI en Codex o Anthropic en Cowork elegida por el despacho, sin anonimización automática. La revisión usa un servidor en el ordenador local. El informe de ejecución describe los datos realmente leídos.
fr: Le modèle peut lire identité de l'entreprise, soldes, mouvements, clients et fournisseurs, créances et dettes, flux prévus, affectations, ajustements, XML facultatifs, prévisions précédentes et décisions du réviseur. L'aperçu initial limite les lignes affichées ; les sources complètes restent lisibles si nécessaire. Python calcule localement sans appeler de services externes ; l'analyse du modèle n'est pas exclusivement locale. Le compte OpenAI dans Codex ou Anthropic dans Cowork choisi par le cabinet s'applique, sans anonymisation automatique. La revue utilise un serveur sur l'ordinateur local. Le rapport d'exécution décrit les données effectivement lues.
it: Il modello può leggere impresa, saldi, movimenti, clienti e fornitori, residui, flussi pianificati, abbinamenti e rettifiche, eventuali XML, previsioni precedenti e decisioni del revisore. L'anteprima iniziale limita il numero di voci visualizzate, ma il modello può leggere le fonti complete quando servono. Python calcola localmente e non chiama servizi esterni; questo non rende locale l'analisi del modello. Si applica l'account OpenAI in Codex o Anthropic in Cowork scelto dallo studio, senza anonimizzazione automatica. La pagina di revisione usa un server sul computer locale. Il report di esecuzione descrive i dati effettivamente letti.

security_controls.control: Each case command requires a current running portable v2 Studio Archive treasury context. Source tables must be exact receipted files within run inputs; traversal and symlinks are rejected. No case outputs are written into the plugin tree.

Source hashes, prepared-input digest, record digest and the pinned artifact inventory are checked on review. Stale writes and concurrent review writes fail; accepted versions cannot be edited in that session.

The review server binds 127.0.0.1, requires an ephemeral token for case API data and exact same-origin headers for writes, serves only declared static assets, and revalidates the archive before every case API request.
Supplied strings are escaped in HTML and assigned with textContent in the review page. Excel text cells are forced to strings and CSV formula prefixes in text columns are escaped.

App-only preparation keeps literal company/currency/cutoff/horizon/coverage, six exact registered CSV/XLSX receipt choices and sheet names, optional extracted XML and an accepted predecessor in atomic actor/tenant/client/engagement/run private drafts with CAS; confirmation is never persisted. Complete source validation and cent-exact arithmetic use unchanged public load_inputs/build_forecast, not inferred source roles. Private pages count every row and display 20 complete parsed rows; oversized pages are refused without sampling. Exact current signed reviewer scope and running run, public preflight and explicit confirmation precede durable intent and public prepare. Retain compiled native manifest and intake, seal every physical file of the immutable first public version, and allow subsequent public date review/acceptance versions only while that initial version and source evidence replay. Identical completed requests replay receipts; uncertain preparation blocks even ordinary view/review. No automatic source-pointer recovery, source rewriting, semantic mapping, anonymization, model/provider/network call, authenticated signature, professional acceptance or Archive completion occurs. Choices, counts and preview cells remain app-private metadata; existing explicit selected-event explanation is the model-context boundary. Host/account processing can still expose locally selected sources when requested.

model_processing.destination: OpenAI model processing used by Codex
Anthropic model processing used by Cowork

external_boundaries.content: Published shared package names and version constraints plus ordinary package-index request metadata. No client files, prompts, case data, credentials, or generated work are sent by this runtime installer.
controls: Only published shared core and explicitly selected OCR recipes are installed; package names are never derived from client material or prompts.

Host network denials stop package retrieval. Retry only the same declared setup after the host user or administrator authorizes registry access; never change host network settings or use an alternate installer to evade a denial.

Readiness probes the managed CPython 3.12 interpreter locally with isolated Python and site loading disabled, checks completed installation metadata, then checks the selected declared package versions and component imports in that interpreter. Recipe revisions, backend bytes and historical platform labels do not block a compatible environment. Compatible reuse leaves installation receipts unchanged; actual missing or incompatible dependencies require serialized repair.
All three products and their modules use the same environment. Optional OCR requires approval and is then retained in that environment. A shared environment is not a boundary between client matters.
external_boundaries.destination: Python Package Index (PyPI) or the package index configured for the active Python interpreter
external_boundaries.purpose: Prepare the published shared Vera, Clara and Lucia core requirements and explicitly approved optional OCR in one user-scoped Python 3.12 environment per operating-system host.
external_boundaries.retention: Packages remain in one fixed user-scoped environment outside plugin source and client folders until explicitly removed. The default location is ~/.local/share/mparanza/runtime/venv on macOS and Linux, and LOCALAPPDATA/mpr/venv on Windows; MPARANZA_RUNTIME_ROOT may override the parent. Enabled OCR remains enabled across later core updates. Package-index request-log retention is controlled by the configured index. Failed updates invalidate the readiness receipt and require repair before execution; this shared environment has no retained generations. Verified temporary code copies are owned by the creating command and removed after completion, failure or cooperative cancellation, with process-exit retry if deletion is temporarily blocked. Preflight verification does not lease a persistent code copy. Installed code, client files and retained professional outputs are not removed. Forced termination or power loss may leave an orphan. On macOS and Linux, fresh code snapshots and native bootstrap copies have private sidecar device/inode records and shared kernel flock leases. Detached native workers inherit the snapshot lease. Normal termination signals stop intake and retain accepted jobs until completion; SIGKILL or power loss can leave copies, recovered on a later verified startup only after an exclusive nonblocking lease proves no holder remains and the directory identity matches. Unmarked historical copies, replaced directories, symlinks and live leases are retained. Lease records contain technical directory identity only, remain outside the indexed code and client folders, and are not returned to the model or sent to a service. Windows retains process-owned cleanup without automatic POSIX orphan recovery. Vera MCP services additionally share a verified immutable code tree keyed by the complete package index hash under the runtime parent/code directory. Kernel leases protect live services; the collector retains two idle releases and never removes client/job state. Active Archive runs retain their original package hash in execution-runtime.json beside their context; reconnects use that verified release while retained. Code storage contains shipped product files only. A missing retired release is explicit and is never silently replaced by newer calculation code. Product service startup and per-run review routing are local and add no external recipient. Native status replies include the technical package hash. The local source installer serializes participating updates and retains the current and previous managed source; direct host updates are outside its lock. Managed CLI command children independently acquire and inherit the same snapshot lease before launch; a terminated launcher cannot release a surviving helper's code. The child keeps that kernel lease until its actual exit. Automatic recovery accepts only lease protocol 2, which guarantees both native-worker and CLI-child inheritance. Older protocol-1 records remain uncollected even without a holder, because legacy helpers may be untracked; current CLI calls may still borrow their leases. Persistent shared-code device/inode metadata is renewed locally after complete package byte verification and a stable identity check during the current verification. This allows filesystem remounts without trusting a stale identity as executable authority. Modified bytes and directory changes during verification remain rejected; unverified replacements do not become eligible for collection. No client content or identity metadata is transmitted by this renewal.

external_boundaries.content: The fixed CPython 3.12 version request, operating-system and architecture selection, and ordinary download request metadata. Setup does not read client files or add prompts, case material or generated reports to this request.
controls: Use an installed CPython 3.12 when available; otherwise use uv or automatically download the published uv 0.12.10 wheel, verify its pinned SHA-256, and provision private CPython 3.12 without changing system Python or shell profiles.
Probe the selected interpreter before creating the dependency environment; never fall back to executing workflows with another Python minor version.
A failed download or interpreter probe stops setup; existing environments and client files remain intact.
external_boundaries.destination: PyPI files.pythonhosted.org for the pinned uv bootstrap, and Astral python-build-standalone CPython distributions on GitHub
external_boundaries.purpose: Provision the single supported CPython 3.12 interpreter when it is absent, automatically bootstrapping uv if needed
external_boundaries.retention: When uv must be bootstrapped, the bootstrap executable and private interpreter remain inside shared runtime storage until removed. Download request-log retention is controlled by the providers.

external_boundaries.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Vera/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis.
controls: Only closed technical transport schemas are accepted; unknown fields and arbitrary recovery commands are rejected.
The fixed HTTPS transport refuses redirects. Reporting failures retain the outbox and do not discard professional outputs.
The remote connector is independent of local command-process startup. If the host cannot expose/connect it, no successful report is claimed.
Only two built-in setup/preparation retries may execute automatically, once per remedy revision. Client documents, ACLs and security settings are not changed.
A published update is not recovery. The failed operation must actually execute successfully before that installation delivery closes.

Supplemental diagnostics require ownership of the original report and matching execution metadata; they are stored separately and cannot change the original report UUID, delivery status or remedy revision. Raw local diagnostic files can only be removed by acknowledging a matching recorded supplement.
Actionable remedies target an explicit original report. Each delivery uses its own applicable revision; a different report with the same generic signal does not inherit that remedy.

A cached actual connector status permits only the two fixed retries for an existing matching local receipt and latest report. It performs no direct HTTP polling or identity adoption. Missing local receipts cannot be fabricated to authorise a retry.

A helper success records readiness. Host AI verification of the original task and inputs is required for all recovered outcomes, including setup/startup. Delayed failures cannot reopen an already recovered episode.
Failed fixed retries retain complete stderr privately for semantic review. Raw recovery stderr is not automatically transmitted.

An explicitly selected MPARANZA_INCIDENT_DELIVERY=local-only setting blocks automatic client HTTP transport for this execution while preserving local evidence. Incident queues are durably marked and not automatically flushed later; this does not make model-provider processing local-only.
external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza HTTPS operational-incident API and Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint
external_boundaries.purpose: Diagnose observed execution/setup failures, return installation-specific remedies and receive actual recovery outcomes
external_boundaries.retention: Local capability, pending reports and receipts persist outside client folders. The service retains incident, report, remedy and outcome records; no automatic deletion period is enforced. Status access is scoped by the opaque capability. Pending diagnostic pointers and raw stderr persist in the private incident directory until a matching actual recorded supplementation receipt is acknowledged; unsuccessful review or delivery retains them. Supplementation never replaces the original recovery episode or reopens recovered records. Recorded original/outcome receipts can acknowledge only their exact local queued UUID without replacing the local capability or saved connector identity. Remedy revisions are retained from the surviving migration revision onward; overwritten legacy revisions are not reconstructed.

security_controls.control: Setup validates package-relative selections and installs the published shared recipe. No package names or dependency instructions are accepted from client documents.
security_controls.on_violation: An unknown module, missing requirements file, invalid target, or failed dependency validation stops the helper instead of executing it in a partial environment.

security_controls.control: One fixed environment is located outside plugin source and client folders. An exclusive operating-system installation lock waits for running managed Python readers, which hold a shared lease through a startup hook. Setup removes the ready receipt before mutation and restores it only after pip check and component validation. Failed setup leaves execution unavailable until repair. Symlink roots, locks and metadata are rejected. The installer is launched from base Python to avoid self-deadlock. This lease is concurrency protection, not a security sandbox. Other historical environments are not automatically deleted. State metadata normally uses atomic replacement. Only EXDEV or Windows error 17 falls back under the same installer lock to a single-link regular-file write with full-byte writes and fsync. Failed writes attempt to restore existing metadata or remove a newly created file; the ready receipt remains invalid until setup succeeds. This fallback is local and does not add a recipient or payload.
security_controls.on_violation: A target creation or validation failure returns a bounded setup error and the requested helper is not run.

security_controls.control: The Windows archive launcher probes a callable interpreter and package entrypoint without changing aliases, registry, execution policy or client folders. The archive helper checks package readability before setup and supplies an explicit task UUID to every managed archive command. Recovery requires reconnecting the selected existing archive root; tasks do not silently adopt each other's configuration. Diagnostics return bounded package/startup status rather than client documents.
security_controls.on_violation: An unreadable package or invalid session stops before runtime setup and archive commands.

security_controls.control: For the six explicitly supported assured modules, the launchers verify the complete package inventory and stable regular-file bytes against the embedded build-generated SHA-256 index. Symlinks, reparse entries, special files, extra directories/files, missing or changed code and unstable reads stop preparation. Unchanged hardlinked package code is materialized into a fresh private OS temporary directory; each copied file is re-read and must have one physical link, then the unchanged component integrity validator must pass. The managed installation and aliases are not modified. The copy contains indexed product code/assets, not client documents, credentials, workflow reports or dependency environments. This local index detects package drift; it is not a publisher signature, a signed origin attestation or proof of installed-host acceptance. The command releases its own temporary code copy after success, failure or cancellation; process-exit cleanup retries pending copies. Ownership is recorded by process ID and directory identity, so borrowed installations, caller paths and replaced roots are not deleted. Forced termination, power loss or persistent file locks can leave an orphan. Cleanup failures log the temporary path and local OS error; they do not add an external recipient or transmit client content. The root-level host .in_use directory is non-executable bookkeeping: only ASCII numeric, ordinary single-link regular marker files are excluded from the product inventory. Nested directories, links, reparse points and non-numeric names there are rejected. Marker contents are not read, executed, transmitted or included in a recovery copy; host markers and installed product files are not modified. On macOS and Linux, fresh code snapshots and native bootstrap copies have private sidecar device/inode records and shared kernel flock leases. Detached native workers inherit the snapshot lease. Normal termination signals stop intake and retain accepted jobs until completion; SIGKILL or power loss can leave copies, recovered on a later verified startup only after an exclusive nonblocking lease proves no holder remains and the directory identity matches. Unmarked historical copies, replaced directories, symlinks and live leases are retained. Lease records contain technical directory identity only, remain outside the indexed code and client folders, and are not returned to the model or sent to a service. Windows retains process-owned cleanup without automatic POSIX orphan recovery. Managed CLI command children independently acquire and inherit the same snapshot lease before launch; a terminated launcher cannot release a surviving helper's code. The child keeps that kernel lease until its actual exit. Automatic recovery accepts only lease protocol 2, which guarantees both native-worker and CLI-child inheritance. Older protocol-1 records remain uncollected even without a holder, because legacy helpers may be untracked; current CLI calls may still borrow their leases.
security_controls.on_violation: Preparation failures and host permission denials stop execution. A failed private copy is removed; no installation chmod/unlink/manual repair, alternate sandbox or relaxed component validation is permitted.

security_controls.control: The parent Vera launcher reports a negative exit code or 137/247 as forced termination. It writes execution_failure.json only inside the selected workflow context output directory or its normalization/sample subdirectories; without that matching context it logs only. The diagnostic stores workflow/run identifiers, exit status and an explicit statement that memory exhaustion is not established by the exit code. It makes no model calls or network requests.
security_controls.on_violation: A worker failure remains failure; diagnostic persistence errors are logged rather than converted into a success.

security_controls.control: The standalone Python bootstrap passes uv only declared host paths, locale, proxy, CA and cache settings, preserving original environment-name casing. Unrelated token/API-key variables and inherited UV_*, VIRTUAL_ENV, CONDA_PREFIX, PYTHONHOME and PYTHONPATH are excluded; private UV_PYTHON_* and UV_CACHE_DIR values are set by the bootstrap. The same environment is used for interpreter discovery and its local probe.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from every bootstrap child process.

security_controls.control: The built-in incident dependency-setup retry uses the shared host/runtime environment allowlist, named runtime/state locations and recovery recursion guard instead of inheriting unrelated user tokens and keys.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from the child environment.

security_controls.control: When the maintained launcher itself runs under Python -I -B, it restores only its own resolved scripts directory for sibling technical-diagnostic imports. It does not add the caller working directory. Helper execution, diagnostic retention and explicit incident delivery policy remain unchanged.
security_controls.on_violation: The maintained launcher must stop rather than resolving technical diagnostics from the caller working directory.

security_controls.control: Review and product MCP services verify the complete package inventory and SHA-256 hashes in their Node process before starting. They have no persistent Python gateway or old-release routing. When Codex installs a component using hardlinks, only that verified component is copied to ordinary single-link temporary files for its existing implementation validator; the bridge removes its copy on normal exit. Forced termination may leave a temporary component copy. No client data, credentials or additional recipients are involved. Native helper jobs retain their separate existing code ownership.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject altered or missing package code before service startup; never alter the host installation.

security_controls.control: When a managed helper carries a selected Archive context, the launcher checkpoints that exact run before and after the helper. Owner-private storage outside the selected archive retains deduplicated admitted inputs, source-receipt snapshots, completed outputs and run headers. It adds local copies with no external upload or automatic deletion. Recovery selects the same IDs and exact byte hashes, retains changed evidence and refuses unrelated destinations. Missing optional checkpoint storage does not hide a committed result or invalidate unchanged available inputs. The selected model may receive checkpoint status, technical identities and local context/output paths from the owning tool; copying bytes itself does not send them to a model. Standalone helpers without Archive context do not create an Archive run.
security_controls.on_violation: Keep the same job and accessible completed work, expose checkpoint availability separately, and recover only from actual verified copies at an authorized destination. Do not claim inaccessible or unsaved bytes were recovered.

external_boundaries.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Vera/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Reporting uses ordinary HTTPS with local capabilities or a browser cookie. Remote MCP endpoints and their OAuth authorization routes are retired. The server stores capability hashes and random owner UUIDs. Previously retained OAuth hashes, callback metadata and reporting records are not deleted by endpoint retirement. No personal account signup, user profile, email or client-file permission is involved. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Installation-preparation failures submit only a fixed technical message, exception type/errno, or the indexed package-relative file name and expected/observed SHA-256 values for a content mismatch. No altered file contents or professional files are read for this report. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis. Current reporting-process version, protocol capabilities and server last-seen time are retained per process session, separately from historical failure versions; they do not establish that all conversations updated. Native-host binding, when invoked, accepts a random host UUID and scoped capability plus an optional explicit native-app label at the same incident service. Only the host capability hash is retained server-side. Stable app-profile UUIDs are derived from host UUID and app label; reporter-instance UUIDs may be task-local and do not count physical computers, plugin copies or people. App grouping grants no additional client status or outcome access. Operator views retain each original report, supplement, outcome and retry event with its actual reporting owner and server receipt time; missing historical task identity is not reconstructed. The native stdio identity bridge verifies its indexed entry, reporter, technical collector and product metadata, then executes an isolated temporary reporter snapshot using existing Python without installing dependencies. Its tool accepts only an existing reporter capability and sends host proof to the fixed register endpoint; it never returns the device key or copies the reporter key into the host identity file. Native broker version/session observations are retained separately from guest reporter and failure-worker observations. When local tools are unavailable, browser reporting depends on the host exposing permitted browser controls. If those controls are absent, delivery remains unverified. Browser identity is distinct from physical-host linkage; no device controls or folder permissions are expanded automatically. Native-helper failures return source-bound exception classes, errno or HTTP status, package-relative frames and developer-authored templates. Dynamic diagnostic values are not returned; unavailable capture is explicit. This bridge does not return raw stderr or device keys. The central recovery agent may request named technical evidence surfaces through a diagnostic-request remedy. The host AI replies with reviewed technical facts, the original report UUID and request revision. Original-task availability is represented by technical booleans, not task text, client identifiers or file contents. A resume remedy communicates a diagnosed correction to the existing authorized workflow; it does not carry executable code. Technical requests, response UUIDs, applicable revisions and their observed status are retained with the original episode. The central agent may implement and deploy incident-related software fixes through reviewed source and green CI under Fabio’s explicit recovery authorization; it does not receive professional case files or gain user-host permissions. Handled Studio Archive exceptions log their active traceback locally before returning the existing error JSON, allowing the same source-bound collector and host semantic review to retain their actual cause. The operator derives diagnostic publication, exact owner/report/revision receipt and reply states, the existing 15-minute deadline and reporting-owner last service contact from retained records. These delivery facts do not establish physical-host availability, diagnosis or original-task recovery. The operator also projects exact delivery, retry and original-task outcome evidence for all actionable remedy kinds, including software updates. Its 15-minute attention cadence is not an execution timeout. A local alert renderer uses technical incident facts and an AI-reviewed blocker, accountable next action, reason and scheduled check. An optional operator-maintained device label is accepted only with a recorded exact-device verification reference; it is not inferred from the recipient, OS or reporter identity. Rendered operator alerts may include opaque machine/case codes and a verified operator-device label, but no client contents, raw diagnostics, personal identifiers or credentials. The renderer neither sends email nor accesses the registry or client files. It rejects stale followup reviews and cannot assign an unreceived or overdue remedy back to the uncontacted Vera. Recovered labels require matching actual original-task success evidence; incomplete historical bindings remain unknown. The shared API also exposes a separate public workflow-testing endpoint: an allowlisted map of pipeline IDs to testing levels and baseline metadata, without incident details, computer IDs, run IDs or user feedback. Its reset is operator-only and does not change incident records. Native workflow transport supplies the same existing host proof during registration when it is available. The shared managed launcher also reports handled PDF recovery failures and subsequent attempts for journal-sampling and journal-bank-reconciliation. It projects fixed strategy/check identifiers, pass/fail/replay flags and attempt/readable-row counts only; PDF text, amounts, paths, adapter code and free-text rationale remain local. Supplements reuse the original report identity across process sessions and cannot certify original-task recovery. Other products carry the shared implementation but do not expose these journal workflows. Bank PDF inspection failures and subsequent corrections are linked per source, independently of journal failures. The bank source digest used in the episode key stays in local reporting state and is not added to transmitted evidence. Other bank statements cannot inherit that extraction recovery. The same native bridge also exposes the fixed task-usage operations documented by the workflow-usage service, with a verified usage-client/catalogue snapshot and task-scoped persistence. Those operations use the existing installation/computer capabilities internally and do not accept credentials, paths, commands or client documents. Error results include SQLite symbolic error codes where available; no raw database contents or diagnostic values are returned. A separate local execution service accepts a published component helper, its argument list, an idempotent job UUID and the retained usage-task UUID. It verifies an indexed code snapshot and invokes the existing managed runtime, without accepting shell expressions or external executable paths. Arguments, complete helper stdout/stderr, job status and cancellation evidence remain in private local execution storage; these can contain case data and are not included in incident HTTP payloads. On a result request, the helper output and status enter the selected host model context through the normal recorded output boundary. Internal collection of stdout is not counted as a model send. Existing subordinate-worker submissions keep their own recording boundary. Native cancellation reads the local OS parent-process graph only to terminate that job and descendants; the graph is neither returned to the model nor uploaded. Native execution and the fixed incident identity/usage broker are separate services. Producer-authored exception measurements may additionally include integer and boolean technical facts with technical identifiers. The Archive state-directory rejection supplies observed POSIX mode, forbidden permission bits, private creation mode, owner/process UID and GID, directory/symlink flags, selection source (explicit, environment or default), and whether creation was requested. It does not transmit the directory path, environment values, client contents, exception arguments or locals. The operator alert displays these facts and package stack coordinates only for its exact original report and linked supplements. The terminal Archive write freezes the local report immediately; a later result from a still-running operation is withheld if its pinned run or revision has closed or changed.

Vera schema 3 requires authenticated installation credentials and an existing physical-machine link. The public anonymous stamping route cannot issue this schema. userID, Archive run ID, revision and report hash are included in the Ed25519 signature.

The request uses one fixed HTTPS operational endpoint. Additional fields, mismatched owner identity, changed retry evidence, wrong-product records and verification mismatches are rejected. Local outgoing payloads are never sent.

Retries retain identical report bytes, UUID, version and revision. Professional artifacts are checked before and after updating only the reserved reporting artifacts in the Archive seal. Ordinary Archive use retries pending receipts and interrupted terminal reporting without re-executing professional work.

Historical schema-1 and schema-2 receipts remain readable through their existing routes; the authenticated Archive proof does not depend on a separate workflow-usage link.

Legacy schema-1 and schema-2 verification remains independent of local installation credentials.

Terminal recovery attempts are isolated and rotated locally; closure occurs after the local report and reseal succeed. Post-tool recording failures return operation, failure stage and a validated opaque run ID where available while withholding unrecorded case content. These metadata acknowledgements add no hosted recipient or server payload field.

Ordinary operations recover only the exact selected client/engagement/run; unrelated pending report locks and server requests are not prerequisites. Explicit maintenance retains the bounded independent recovery queue. Execution, completion and professional-artifact seals retain their full integrity checks. No new recipient, payload field or source-file transmission is introduced.
